mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen for three consecutive weeks from -71.1 to -67.4, indicating a self-reinforcing behavioral adaptation to lockdown conditions (e.g. click-and-collect routines, essential-plus trips). This momentum is expected to continue, producing a higher 4-week mean for RETAIL_REC relative to the prior 4 weeks.
evidence_refs: fact: RETAIL_REC increased in each of the last three weekly observations
failure_condition: The next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is equal to or lower than the trailing 28-day mean despite three or more consecutive weekly increases preceding the decision point.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility is recovering faster than other categories, moving from -28.7 to -21.3 over three weeks. Once GROCERY_PHARM crosses above -20, it signals that essential-trip normalization is spilling over into broader non-essential retail behavior, lifting RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above -20 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact: GROCERY_PHARM improved by 7.4 points over three weeks, the fastest recovering category
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise in the two weeks following any week in which GROCERY_PHARM first exceeds -20, observed in a majority of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous week-on-week increases in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT jointly indicate resumption of commuting routines, which generates incidental retail footfall near transit hubs and workplaces beyond what either series would predict alone, raising RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT increase week-on-week simultaneously for 2 consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact: WORKPLACES improved from -55.6 to -54.0 and TRANSIT roughly stabilized near -68 to -70 over the snapshot window
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next 28-day mean does not exceed its trailing 28-day mean even though WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rose concurrently for two or more weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Under a regime of continued national lockdown paired with an active vaccine rollout, a slight decline in RESIDENTIAL (23.0 to 22.1) signals early loosening of strict stay-at-home compliance ahead of formal policy easing, which precedes and predicts a rise in RETAIL_REC over the following four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact: RESIDENTIAL declined for three consecutive weeks from 23.0 to 22.1
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next 28-day mean is not higher than its trailing 28-day mean despite RESIDENTIAL declining in the prior three weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Late-winter weather volatility drives erratic week-to-week swings in PARKS (-17.7, -25.6, -21.7, -20.6) that reflect substitution between outdoor recreation and indoor retail visits. When PARKS mobility rises sharply week-on-week due to a mild-weather spell, some recreation demand is diverted away from retail venues, suppressing RETAIL_REC in the immediate following week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact: PARKS showed a non-monotonic pattern with an 8-point weekly swing between t-3w and t-2w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall in the week following a greater-than-5-point week-on-week rise in PARKS, observed across a majority of such occurrences.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility falling below a 22.0 percent-change threshold indicates measurably reduced time spent at home, which is directly associated with increased outside-the-home activity including retail and recreation visits, raising RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 22.0 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact: RESIDENTIAL reached 22.1 at t-0w, just above the 22.0 threshold
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's 2-week forward mean does not increase relative to its trailing mean in instances where RESIDENTIAL subsequently falls below 22.0.

mechanism_narrative: Joint increases in GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS reflect a broader public willingness to leave home for multiple purposes in a single outing; this combined effect synergistically increases incidental retail-and-recreation visits (errand-chaining behavior) beyond the additive effect of either series alone, raising RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: both GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS increase in the same week
evidence_refs: fact: GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS both increased at t-0w relative to t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next 28-day mean does not exceed its trailing 28-day mean in periods where GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS rose concurrently in the same week.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has shown a small but steady recovery from -55.6 to -54.0 over three weeks, reflecting incremental return of in-person workers. This incremental commuting activity directly boosts adjacent lunchtime and after-work retail visits, producing a modest rise in RETAIL_REC in the immediately following week.
evidence_refs: fact: WORKPLACES improved each week from -55.6 to -54.0 across the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week immediately following any week where WORKPLACES improved, observed in a majority of such instances.
